sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Statutory Company Secretarial and Commercial Registered Agent Office

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid_Civil_Law (French-inspired civil law codices with Germanic company-law elements; unitary national legal order)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU (Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union) network of more than 90 Bilateral Investment Treaties
Luxembourg-Germany Double Tax Avoidance Agreement (23 August 2012)
Luxembourg-United States Double Tax Avoidance Agreement (1996, as amended by 2009 Protocol incorporating FATCA IGA)
EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement and EU-CETA (Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement with Canada, applied provisionally since 2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (SARL provisions, Art. 710-1 et seq.; registered office, Art. 100-2 et seq.); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and on Company Accounts, as amended (RCS); Law of 12 November 2004 on the Fight against Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT; Law of 2 September 2011 on Access to the Professions (business authorization); Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961 (in force for Luxembourg since 4 April 1979)
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (RBE mandatory registration; direct access for Luxembourg FIU, CSSF, notaries and AML-obliged entities; public access only upon demonstrated legitimate interest after CJEU judgment C-37/20 and C-601/20 and national implementing amendments)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each UBO, director and manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing passport authority / certifying notary in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (all Apostille Convention members) or Consular Legalization (non-member states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing and register extract of any corporate shareholder (where applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry / official commercial registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; sworn translation into French if issued in non-Latin script

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds evidence for the minimum capital deposit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of bank officer; apostille only if required by the receiving Luxembourg bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney in favor of the Luxembourg notary and domiciliation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Grantor / certifying notary in the signatory's home jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based AML/CFT program per CSSF Regulation 12-02: (i) CDD before service commencement; (ii) identification of all UBOs at the 25% threshold; (iii) mandatory PEP screening covering domestic/foreign PEPs, family members and known close associates; (iv) name-screening against the UN Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists (Reg. 2580/2001 and Reg. 269/2010), OFAC SDN list for USD-linked flows, and FATF public statements; (v) enhanced due diligence, including source of wealth/source of funds verification for PEP and high-risk clients; (vi) reporting obligations to the Luxembourg FIU (Cellule de Renseignement Financier); (vii) ongoing transaction monitoring and periodic re-screening at least annually.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - official platform www.lbr.lu integrating the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés); name availability pre-check via the LBR portal and final judicial confirmation by the drafting notary
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be composed in Latin script and kept in the RCS in their original form with diacritics; a name in any language (French, German, Luxembourgish, English or other Latin-script language) is admissible provided it is distinctive and not misleading. The corporate suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' (or 's.a r.l.') must appear for limited-liability identification. Names must not create confusion with existing RCS entries, protected trademarks, or international organizations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank, Bancaire (requires CSSF prior authorization for regulated financial institutions)
Assurance, Insurance, Réassurance (regulated insurance terms requiring regulatory approval)
OPC, SICAV, SICAF, Fonds d'investissement (collective investment scheme terms requiring CSSF licensing)
PSF, PFS, Société de domiciliation, Trust, Fiduciaire (reserved regulated activities without a valid professional authorization)
Réviseur d'entreprises, Expert-comptable, Avocat, Notaire (reserved liberal professions)
Luxembourg, État, Grand-Duché, Ministère, Commune (misleading connection with the State; prior Ministry of State approval required)
Europe, Union européenne (in a misleading or institutionally suggestive manner)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No administrative extension of the standard name pre-clearance window exists; a fresh availability check and reservation must be run before the notarial deed if the 30-day window lapses. Upon rejection, the applicant may (i) re-file with additional distinctive elements through the LBR portal; (ii) file a reasoned written appeal with the RCS registrar within 15 working days of the refusal; (iii) bring an appeal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within 2 months of the final administrative refusal, supported by evidence of prior use, absence of confusion or trademark rights.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as sole office. The SARL must maintain a physical registered office in Luxembourg, staffed on a business-day basis, as required by the Law of 10 August 1915 and the Ministry of the Economy business authorization under the Law of 2 September 2011. For a licensed registered-agent/secretarial company, virtual-office services may only supplement the physical office; if domiciliation for regulated entities (PSF/CI) is envisaged, a CSSF-supervised domiciliation licence with dedicated substance is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 18 months for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced licensed secretarial company; probability rises above 50% where the company provides domiciliation or offshore-client mandates without dedicated staff, premises and records.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial fees for the notarized deed of incorporation of the SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory graduated notarial tariff schedule (Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 March 2009) based on subscribed capital and deed annexes

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory minimum subscribed share capital deposit held in notary escrow (EUR 12,000 subscribed; 25% partially paid at incorporation, recoverable as corporate asset)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory minimum capital requirement under the Law of 10 August 1915 (Art. 710-5 et seq.)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS incorporation filing and registration fee via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS fee schedule for the filing of the notarial deed and incorporation dossier

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation deed in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / LBR publication office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RESA publication tariff per deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Ministry of the Economy business authorization (Autorisation d'établissement) application handling via local trade agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministère de l'Économie / authorized local agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Public filing fee zero; agency handling fee at prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce registration and first-year compulsory membership
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Chamber by-law subscription scale for commercial registrants

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation contract (12-month term) with commercial substance support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 100-140 per month for a physical registered office and substance support

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT onboarding: UBO piercing, PEP/OFAC/UN sanctions screening database subscription and initial CDD file build
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Vendor subscription and flat compliance-support fee (market benchmark)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation of English/source-language corporate documents into French for RCS and CSSF filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory sworn-translator tariff per page (market benchmark)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of UBO and shareholder documents (3 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Apostille/consular authority of the documents' country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Origin-country statutory apostille/consular fee; USD 100-150 per document benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank pre-incorporation account opening and KYC compliance dossier fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank compliance fee at prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel for due diligence, drafting of articles of association, UBO register filing and anti-money-laundering gap analysis
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat-fee engagement at prevailing market benchmark of USD 2,500-4,000 for Stage 1

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, particularly Articles 710-1 to 710-27 for Société à Responsabilité Limitée; registration under Articles 18 and 20 of the same law.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), attached to the Luxembourg District Court.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (notarial deed of incorporation) filed electronically through the RCS portal (lbr.lu) and published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SARL minimum share capital is EUR 12,000, which must be fully subscribed and paid in cash before registration. The amount is blocked in a Luxembourg credit institution escrow account or a notary client escrow account and released to the company only after RCS registration. Contributions in kind require a statutory auditor's special report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by the founders and the first management board, that the SARL's incorporation is approved and its initial share capital of EUR 12,000 has been fully subscribed and paid in. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office is established at the address in the Articles, and the manager is authorized to complete RCS registration and publication. FURTHER RESOLVED that [Person A] is appointed sole manager and [Person B] deputy manager, with signing authority as set out in the Articles. FINALLY RESOLVED that all regulatory applications for the licensed registered-agent and secretarial business, including notarization and licence filings, are ratified and delegated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Luxembourg notary to prepare the statuts. The founders must agree on corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose covering registered-agent and secretarial services, initial capital and first managers. The incorporation deed is executed before the notary by all founders or by a holder of a notarized and apostilled power of attorney. The notary submits the deed for registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized power of attorney for each representative founder
Valid passport or identity card of each founder and manager
Declaration of non-bankruptcy and good repute for each manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries a conflict between the stated corporate purpose and the regulated activity, the notary amends the purpose limitation clause and re-executes the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Capital Escrow and Obtain Bank Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or notary client escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked pre-incorporation account in the name of the future SARL and deposit EUR 12,000. The bank issues a capital certificate or escrow confirmation stating that the funds are irrevocably reserved for incorporation. The certificate is delivered to the notary for attachment to the incorporation dossier and release after registration.
required_dossiers: Bank statement or escrow certificate evidencing EUR 12,000 deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank KYC requests additional evidence, provide source-of-wealth documentation and a statutory declaration from the ultimate beneficial owner; if declined, select another Luxembourg bank and re-issue the escrow certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial deed, statutes, capital certificate, manager declarations and completed RCS filing forms through the RCS electronic filing portal, or have the notary transmit them. Pay the official filing fee. RCS performs legal-form conformity review and assigns the registration number.
required_dossiers: Funds-blocking certificate from the bank or notary escrow
Manager acceptance declarations and signature specimens
Proof of payment of official registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RCS issues a query, cure the stated legal deficiency within the notified deadline by filing supplemental declarations or re-notarizing an amended deed; failure to cure leads to deemed lapse and a new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), managed by the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the notary files the statutory extract for mandatory publication in RESA. The publication gives the incorporation deed binding effect against third parties and completes the legal formation publicity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or contains errors, the notary submits a corrective filing with RCS and re-publishes within ten days; third-party reliance is avoided retroactively where legally permissible.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax, Social Security and Precursory Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA; Administration des contributions directes; Centre commun de la sécurité sociale; Ministry of the Economy and CSSF where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File VAT and corporate income tax registration, register the manager and any employees for social security, and file the statutory UBO declaration. Simultaneously apply for the commercial establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) and, if the registered-agent activity is financial-sector regulated, the CSSF professional-of-the-financial-sector authorisation.
required_dossiers: CSSF PSF/CTSP application files, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licensing authority requires further fit-and-proper evidence, submit the manager's curriculum vitae, criminal-record extract, detailed organizational chart and shareholder structure; an administrative appeal may be filed within three months of refusal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie (Direction générale des PME) for the commercial establishment permit; Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for regulated corporate service-provider and registered-agent activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement under the amended Law of 28 December 1988 on the exercise of independent professions, together with, where applicable, a CSSF licence as a Professional of the Financial Sector for domiciliation and corporate secretarial services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for office-only secretarial activity; no industrial production installations requiring a full EIA report or integrated environmental permit under the IED class.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process effluent or combustion emissions; sanitary wastewater only, connected to the municipal network and compliant with Luxembourg effluent-discharge limits; waste handling under national waste classification and WEEE rules for electronic media and office equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification from the municipal fire-protection service; occupancy permit for the commercial office premises; workplace compliance inspection by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering electrical safety, ventilation, lighting, ergonomics and emergency evacuation; civil-defence emergency plan where the headcount threshold is exceeded.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) — direct corporate income, municipal business, net wealth and payroll taxes (6, rue de la Congrégation, L-2411 Luxembourg); Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — VAT, registration duties and excise duties (6, rue Coudenhove-Kalergi, L-1359 Luxembourg). Electronic portals: Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu), MyGuichet/Guichet.lu and the ACD/AEDT secure taxpayer portal (tax.lu, eSpace professionnel).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a new SARL: (1) notary transcribes the incorporation deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); (2) LBR/RCS enrolment automatically allocates the 13-digit national identification number (matricule), which serves as the direct-tax file number; (3) the SARL files the VAT commencement declaration (déclaration de commencement d'activité) with the AEDT via MyGuichet within 15 days of commencement, attaching the RCS extract; (4) the AEDT assigns the LU + 8-digit VAT number (typically 5 to 10 business days); (5) non-resident entities with a Luxembourg fixed establishment file a PE/registration declaration with the ACD and register with the AEDT under the non-established taxpayer procedure, appointing an approved fiscal representative where required. The SARL, as a resident company, must hold a valid matricule before any taxable invoice is issued.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Luxembourg SARL is per se a resident corporate taxpayer for CIT (17% + 7% solidarity surcharge = 18.19% federal-equivalent), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal, standard ~6.75% in Luxembourg City; aggregate ordinary-income burden ≈ 24.94%) and net wealth tax (0.5% on taxable net wealth). It exercises worldwide taxation with foreign tax credit/exemption and, where the 10%/12-month participation conditions are met, the SOPARFI participation exemption. There is no transparent/pass-through election available to a SARL; the owning shareholders are taxed only on distributions (15% withholding, unless treaty-reduced).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box is available. Statutory elections: (1) Article 164bis LIR fiscal unity (unlimited joint consolidated CIT) for ≥95%-held resident subsidiaries, requiring prior ACD application and minimum 5-year period; (2) VAT group election under the 1979 VAT law (single taxable person for intra-group supplies); (3) SOPARFI status (not an election but a qualifying participation exemption using conditions of 10% holding/12-month holding and no non-taxable CIV requirement); (4) option to tax real-property leases for registered-office premises; (5) ATAD I/II hybrid mismatch and interest limitation elections and PE recharacterization under the Law of 20 December 2019; (6) partial deduction/pro-rata VAT election for mixed-use activities. None of these elections alter the entity-level classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA — Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) under the Loi du 12 février 1979, transposing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC and Directive (EU) 2020/285 on small-business and OSS simplification.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 (no threshold). Any taxable person supplying goods or services in Luxembourg — resident or non-resident — must register with the AEDT before the first taxable transaction. Luxembourg does not apply an incorporable small-enterprise 'franchise en base' exemption; a non-established supplier may, instead of local VAT registration, use the OSS/IOSS mechanism for qualifying cross-border B2C digital services, subject to the conditions of the 2019 VAT e-commerce package.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, transactional reporting or digital stamping applies to B2B invoicing in Luxembourg. E-invoicing is mandatory only for invoices issued to Luxembourg public administrations and public undertakings (e-Factura via PEPPOL network, PEPPOL BIS 3.0/UBL formats; public procurement); B2B e-invoicing is optional with recipient consent. Tax records must be kept 10 years in conformity with the VAT law; upon request, the AEDT may demand SAF-T type audit files. Intrastat/EC Sales List (Liste récapitulative) and periodic TVA returns are filed electronically through the tax.lu portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% (exonération à l'exportation) applies when the exporter proves physical dispatch to a third-country destination within 90 days of supply and holds the customs export declaration (SAD/MRN). Services: corporate-secretarial and registered-agent services supplied B2B follow the customer's place of business (Article 58 of the VAT law): non-EU taxable customers place the service outside Luxembourg's territorial scope (effective 0%); intra-EU taxable customers allow a zero-rated invoice provided the customer's VAT ID is validated, the service is not caught by domestic use-and-enjoyment rules, and the EC Sales List is filed. Supplies to private (B2C) non-EU clients are taxable in Luxembourg unless the effective-use-and-enjoyment exception applies; digital services to non-EU consumers can use OSS/IOSS. Full economic substance documentation must evidence that the secretarial fees are genuine and not a shell/offshore-conduit recharacterization target.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD — Single Administrative Document) with assigned MRN evidencing EU exit, filed via Luxembourg Customs or the other EU exit customs office
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note proving physical dispatch of goods from EU customs territory to a third country
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 arrival confirmation showing export proceeds credited to the SARL's Luxembourg bank account within the FX repatriation deadline
Commercial contract, purchase order and final export invoice cross-referenced to the declaration
Audit file reconciling each 0% invoice to customs exit proof, transport documents and payment rails
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT may reopen files for 5 years (10 years on proven fraud). Unsubstantiated or fraudulent 0% claims are clawed back as Luxembourg VAT at 17% plus interest of 0.6% per month, and the taxpayer is exposed to an administrative fine of 10%-100% of the evaded tax. Recharacterization of artificial 'registered-agent/secretarial' conduits can generate withholding tax, net-wealth tax and ATAD consequences; forged export documents expose directors to criminal penalties up to EUR 1,000,000 and up to 5 years' imprisonment. Export proof must be contemporaneous; incomplete files at the audit notice are automatically disallowed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (Central Bank of Luxembourg, BCL)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a eurozone member state; the euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. The EU Treaty guarantees free movement of capital; no general exchange control regime applies. Profit remittance is unrestricted, subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and, for certain outbound dividends, potential withholding tax relief under EU Directives, the Luxembourg-Netherlands tax treaty network, or the participation exemption regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no mandatory export proceeds surrender requirement and no foreign exchange repatriation or conversion obligation on receivables in any currency.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. A non-EU digital electronic money institution (EMI) cannot operate in Luxembourg without obtaining a licence from the CSSF or passporting a valid EEA EMI licence under PSD2. Such EMIs are generally accepted as ancillary banking channels but face additional AML/KYC equal-to-bank requirements and may be viewed as a higher compliance risk for a registered-agent/secretarial service entity holding third-party funds. Onshore licensed EMIs (e.g., licensed by CSSF or passported) are preferred for clients, while operational clearing activity remains best routed through tier-1 banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors may technically open accounts remotely via notarised powers of attorney and advanced electronic identification, but most Luxembourg tier-1 banks require at least one physical appearance or a personal, in-person interview of a senior director or ultimate beneficial owner for medium-risk corporate clients, particularly those in the company-service-provider sector. Non-resident directors without local substance may be asked to provide a physical Luxembourg registered agent for attendance if they cannot travel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered-agent/secretarial client base composed of non-resident managed entities with no economic substance in Luxembourg
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate registry extract (RCS), ultimate beneficial ownership declaration, audited financial statements of parent, description of actual commercial activities, evidence of tax residency, and a substance memo compliant with Luxembourg tax and CSSF circular guidance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual or unexplained high-velocity wire activity through operational account, especially to non-EU jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transactional trail, signed engagement letters for each client, underlying service invoices, evidence of proper AML/CDD files, periodic compliance review reports, and confirmations of corresponding external counsel onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder or director appears on PEP or sanctions screening lists, or is subject to EU restrictive measures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent PEP/sanctions screening output, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements, notarised identity documents, proof of family relationship where relevant, legal opinions on such exposure, and a remediation plan approved by the designated director of the SARL.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed via SWIFT wire (typically MT103) with accurate purpose codes under BCL/ECB balance-of-payments statistical reporting. For a Luxembourg SARL, shareholder loans or equity injections should reference purpose codes such as 'S0022' (direct investment – equity capital) or appropriate EBOPS classification, and the bank instruction must reference the registered office and RCS number. The receiving bank must verify the mandate, the underlying BCL declaration obligation, and the corporate authorisation (resolution of the general meeting).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for trade or service obligations are effected primarily through SWIFT MT103/MT202 messages in EUR or convertible currencies, subject to normal anti-money-laundering and sanctions screening. Commercial letters of credit are not typical for pure company secretarial services but remain permissible where the underlying engagement involves documentary trade support; otherwise standard bank wire and electronic payment systems are the principal clearing rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted-currency exposures (if counterparty approved)
FX options (plain vanilla calls and puts)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and management report (comptes annuels et rapport de gestion)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after financial year-end; a calendar-year SARL must file by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court summons by the RCS to regularise; administrative fine up to EUR 25,000; repeated non-filing triggers judicial strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the entity's UBO registration date; shareholding changes are disclosed at the same interval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 125,000 per violation and possible daily penalty until correction; register freeze affects transactions, not company strike-off directly.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax and municipal business tax return (déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités et d'impôt commercial communal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Paper filing by 30 June of the year after the tax year; electronic filing (MyGuichet/eTVA) is conventionally accepted until 31 December of that following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-interest at 0.6% of unpaid tax plus late-payment surcharge up to 10% of assessed amount.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax declaration (impôt sur la fortune, integrated with annual income tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual CIT/MBT return using the same 30 June / 31 December filing calendar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessment by ACD with 0.6% monthly late interest; refusal of tax residence certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT annual reconciliation declaration (déclaration annuelle TVA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May following the VAT accounting period for monthly/quarterly filers submitting through the eTVA portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of EUR 100-500 and VAT late-interest at 0.6% per month; withholding of tax clearance for public procurement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual social security declaration of wages (déclaration annuelle de la sécurité sociale – DAS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January following the calendar year in which wages were paid; nil declaration required if payroll treated as nil.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 2,500 for late/incorrect submission; recalculated social contributions plus interest.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises) when it exceeds two of three thresholds: balance-sheet total EUR 4.4m, net turnover EUR 8.8m, and 50 employees on average; public-interest entities are audited irrespective of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Plan comptable général luxembourgeois) as implemented by the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts, aligned with EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS is optional for unlisted and mandatory for listed/consolidated entities under Art. 55ter of the 1915 Companies Law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The RBE declaration must list every natural person directly or indirectly holding more than 25% of capital or voting control, including the source of ownership. Within 30 days of any transfer that changes beneficial ownership or its percentages, the entity files an amended declaration; a zero-change annual confirmation is due within 30 days of the RBE registration anniversary.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of members / nominal shares register
Register of share transfers and pledges
Minute book of shareholders' and managers' meetings
Register of managers/directors with service details

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 3,200 - 6,000 per annum for registered-office and secretarial-agent services in Luxembourg City, excluding notarial or government filing disbursements.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 14,000 for an unlisted SARL with a calendar-year closing, including tax-return tie-in work and RCS publication support.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate income tax rate in Luxembourg City (17% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge on the corporate income tax, and 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Intellectual property box exempts 80% of qualifying IP income, yielding an effective rate near 5.20%; notional interest deduction on qualifying new equity; R&D tax credits; investment tax credits; incentive available for financing and IP holding structures, though standard corporate secretarial services have limited ordinary deductions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modèle 300 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed jointly with Modèle 400 (Municipal Business Tax Return) through the MyGuichet.lu secured portal or via an approved professional e-filing channel; Luxembourg tax identification number required
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Must be filed by 31 May of the year following the tax year when the fiscal year coincides with the calendar year; for a non-calendar fiscal year, the return is due before the expiry of the fifth calendar month following the fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification: registered legal name, Luxembourg RCS number, address, legal form SARL, tax file number, and fiscal representative details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the non-resident shareholder’s address and appoint a Luxembourg tax agent for service of process if no seat in Luxembourg

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss-offset: net commercial profit or loss per statutory financial statements, adjusted for Luxembourg-specific corrections and tax-base reclassifications
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Luxembourg-source income and expenses attributable to the Luxembourg permanent establishment or registered activity; attach a statement reconciling the Luxembourg scope from the global accounts

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenditures: taxes on income, fines, criminal penalties, excessive or undocumented board fees, excessive interest under thin-capitalisation rules, and intra-group charges not at arm’s length
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back any Luxembourg-source non-deductible items; do not allocate foreign head-office overheads unless supported by a written cost-sharing agreement

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and preferential regimes: net wealth tax forming an expense, notional interest deduction, R&D tax credit, IP box benefit, and foreign tax credits for underlying Luxembourg-source profits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty foreign-tax-credit relief only when the documentary evidence, including the tax residence certificate and source-country tax assessment, is annexed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration signature and certification: legal representative’s electronic signature, date, and confirmation that the return is complete and accurate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Luxembourg appointed tax agent or resident manager must sign; power of attorney and all supporting schedules must be submitted in the same e-filing package

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete filing attracts default assessment and administrative penalty up to 10% of the final tax due; late payment interest accrues at 0.8% per month; continued non-compliance can trigger publication of the tax claim and enforcement measures

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg withholding tax on shareholder dividends; 0% for qualifying distributions under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or domestic participation exemption when the shareholder holds at least 10% for an uninterrupted 12-month period (or is a qualifying EU parent), subject to beneficial-ownership and substance requirements
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke double-taxation agreement relief, the beneficial owner must submit a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the residence jurisdiction and a Form DTR/Lux withholding relief application to the Luxembourg tax administration or paying agent; for EU directive relief, a self-declaration confirming eligible shareholder status, 10% shareholding, and holding period must be provided; the Luxembourg withholding agent must retain the documentation, and a refund path is available when relief was not granted at source
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% domestic withholding tax unless reduced to 0% for EU associated companies under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive or lowered under an applicable treaty; interest: no Luxembourg domestic withholding tax on ordinary commercial interest (0% statutory), though treaty-dependent limitations and anti-abuse rules apply

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required where aggregate related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000 per fiscal year; Master File required when the group’s consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 50,000,000; Country-by-Country Report threshold is the OECD/EU EUR 750,000,000 group consolidated revenue
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a separate Economic Substance Regulations ordinance, but the domestic anti-abuse provision in Article 56 LIR, EU ATAD interest-limitation and controlled-foreign-corporation rules, and OECD/HJSO substance concepts require the SARL to maintain real presence, personnel, offices, independent decision-making, and profit-bearing activity; professional corporate secretarial and registered-agent service providers must demonstrate commercial substance to secure treaty benefits, participation exemption, and the Interest and Royalties Directive

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Luxembourg-source income, issuing false invoices for secretarial services, concealing ultimate beneficial ownership, or using fabricated deductions to reduce taxable profit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of all hidden income, penalty up to twice the evaded tax, criminal fines up to EUR 250,000, and imprisonment up to five years for responsible natural persons
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally and jointly liable for the corporate tax liability and penalties when they knowingly sign false returns or participate in a shell invoicing scheme; criminal proceedings can impose director imprisonment, freezing orders, and travel bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company Without Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the SARL as a letter-box company solely to claim treaty benefits, receive passive royalties, or route dividends without any physical presence, staff, or operational management in Luxembourg
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty and directive relief, disallowance of the participation exemption, recharacterisation under Article 56 LIR, additional taxation at the 24.94% rate, plus civil penalties of 10% or more on underpaid corporate income tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for the unpaid tax and penalties when they authorise the artificial structure; the corporate veil may be pierced if the entity is a mere facade, leading to personal attachment and restrictive measures

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Beneficial Ownership Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: As a registered-agent and corporate-secretarial provider, failing to identify and verify ultimate beneficial owners, failing to maintain required records, omitting the Luxembourg beneficial ownership register filing, or ignoring suspicious transaction indicators
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines for legal persons up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover; regulatory suspension or withdrawal of the professional licence; publication of the sanction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face personal criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years for wilful AML breaches; civil liability for damages to investors or the Luxembourg State attaches where fraudulent facilitation caused a loss

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Persistent Late Filing and Obstruction of Tax Control
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repeated failure to file Form 300/400, refusing to provide transfer-pricing documentation or underlying vouchers, obstructing tax audits, and refusing to pay assessed Luxembourg taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Default assessment, late-filing penalty up to 10% of tax, monthly late-payment interest at 0.8%, coercive fines by the liquidation committee, and forced recovery against assets
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be stripped of the benefit of limited liability where the failure to file or pay amounts to intentional fraudulent non-compliance; Luxembourg courts can impose director liability for the entire unpaid corporate tax, travel bans, and up to two years of imprisonment for defiance of fiscal authorities
